Founded 2025, Turtle Net is a social media site built around turtles and tortoises. The CSS and styling are mid-2000s themed. Users, called "Turtle Club members", can upload turtle-related images and videos, comment, and more.

Other than just being a social media, Turtle Net has grown into a learning resource, with articles related to turtles and other marine life.

TurtleWave Search (formerly TurtleWave Browser until 2024) is a search engine created in 2023 by 'BayTurtleKing' with the help of 'KazWasTaken'. It began in May 2023 as TurtleWave Browser, a website (not a web browser) that was the home of TurtleWave Search. Its first version, V1, was hosted on Glitch and served as a simpler, privacy-safe alternative to larger search engines. It ranked results from a manually maintained log of sites, which started in September 2023 and reached nearly 1000 sites by the end of its life. It added detection for typos in the user search query during keyword result matching.

Over the course of two years, V1 was continuously updated. Accounts, backgrounds, light mode, style options, and a "Feeling lucky" button (later removed) arrived in late 2023. In spring 2024 it added an odd JavaScript modification creator, much customization, image results, a helper bot that gave pre made answers, and Wikipedia facts, followed by easter egg searches and a Search Manager for switching search engines that May. The site's title changed to TurtleWave Search in August 2024, and after a quiet stretch in late 2024, development picked back up in early 2025 with a UI revamp. It was also released as a Windows app, an Android app, and a browser extension (which still exists but brings you to V2). A Glitch outage took it offline in March 2024 and again in December 2024, when a 10 day outage went into January 2025. In February 2025, several websites falsely labeled it a virus because of ads it never had.

On May 22, 2025, it was announced that the site would be deleted in exactly six weeks because Glitch was shutting down, leaving a hard choice about whether to find a new host and buy a domain and keep it going, or to just archive it all. When Glitch shut down in 2025, the search engine and all TurtleWave websites were discontinued. It came back in late 2025 on Netlify at turtlewave.netlify.app, however some features were missing or broken.

TurtleWave Search V2 was released in mid-2026 at search.turtlewave.dev and was made from the ground up. Compared to V1, it offers better results, an improved interface, and less bloat. A major update in late 2026 added new widgets, better image search, and more safety features. TurtleWave Search is also available as a search engine option in Shell Surfer, a browser made by the same creator.

TurtleWave Music (V1) was a simple music player created in 2024 and originally built into TurtleWave Search V1. Hosted on Glitch, it was essentially just an HTML audio player using manually referenced Internet Archive files. It was discontinued in mid 2025 and fully taken down when Glitch shut down. It came back when TurtleWave moved to Netlify, but only showed the old shutdown message.

TurtleWave Music V2 was created in early 2026 with two halves: a radio browser using various online radio sources, and a cleaner interface than Internet Archive's own for searching and playing its albums, tracks, and recordings. The radio browser was later added to the Shell Surfer web browser as 'SSurf Radio'. Compared to V1, V2 offers the entire Internet Archive library, online radio stations, and a much more modern UI.

Shell Surfer (or SSurf) is a heavily customizable and configurable, Electron-based web browser made as part of TurtleWave. Its earliest versions, 1.4R and older, were tiny and barely functioned as web browsers. 1.5R added a basic tab and bookmark feature, and 1.6R, released in May 2026, had the browser completely built from the ground up with better tabs, bookmarks in the tool bar, a context menu, Reader Mode, and protcol support (like ssurf://).

Over the next the 1.x updates, it added an extension system with an official store and built in extension maker, support for some Chrome and Firefox extensions, AdBlock, parental controls, many safety and security features, and five separate built-in UI styles a user could choose from. Other later updates include additions like find in page, spell check, website history, a built-in notepad, an internet radio page (SSurf Radio, powered by TurtleWave Music Radio), a password manager, and ways to transfer data from other browsers.

Shell Surfer began as a Windows only browser with .exe installers, then moved to an .msi installer in 1.9.4R. Linux support for many distros arrived in 1.12.1R.
